findings.title: Fulfillment before satisfaction
findings.claim: The confirmed good can be trusted before its felt adequacy arrives: fulfillment remains ahead of satisfaction, so confirmation carries a temporal lag.
findings.mechanism: The focus fulfillment and utmost-limit facets meet the future satisfaction surface at 92:21; the attributed satisfaction branches provide the separate affective and relational trigger that makes the present confirmation point toward later closure.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive confirmation as a commitment made before the final feeling of adequacy, with later satisfaction completing rather than replacing the present act.
findings.containment: This keeps the ordinary good and future reward readings together; it does not make delayed satisfaction the only meaning.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT trace supplies the future marker, focus return, before/after change, and alternative; both context satisfaction branches remain unresolved and attributed.
